_comment: KNOWN-ESCALATED TRACKED-FILE DIFFS — the fifth gap shape of skills/session-inheritance-audit/scripts/check_round_recorded.py (round 373, harness A), read by load_escalated_diffs/classify_escalated_diffs. This registry is NOT state/known-standing-dirty-paths.json and must never be used as one. That file models UNTRACKED files a separate autonomous system permanently leaves behind, and its entries are unconditional. This one models a TRACKED file that system EDITED, where a round has already inspected the diff, decided, and the decision was to leave it uncommitted and escalate. Round 349 refused to allowlist exactly this case on the grounds that doing so 'would mean never look at this diff again, which is the wrong answer' — that refusal is honoured here by making every entry CONTENT-PINNED: worktree_blob is `git hash-object` of the file as it sits in the tree, head_blob is `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>`. The acknowledgement holds only while BOTH still match. If the third party edits the file again, or a commit moves the base underneath it, the pin expires by itself and the checker reports the path LOUDER than an ordinary unattributed one. If the path stops being dirty at all the entry is reported as dead and must be DELETED — an acknowledgement that suppresses nothing reads as coverage. Adding an entry is an assertion that a specific round inspected THIS EXACT DIFF and recorded its reasoning somewhere findable; `reason` must name that round's artifact. Re-pinning after a change requires a fresh inspection, not a hash update.
_suite_neutral_note: `suite_neutral` is read by harness/pristine_check.py's escalation_allowed_dirty and by NOTHING else. It answers pristine-check rule 1's question ('could this dirty file have changed a suite's outcome?'), which is a different question from 'has this diff been adjudicated?'. Omit it unless a round has actually checked; absent/false means the path keeps blocking the pristine differential, which is the safe default.

languages/whence/SECURITY.md.why_the_entry_was_deleted: HEAD and the working tree are both the pinned base 929c52c42523: the Hermes gateway rewrote its own edit away at 2026-09-04T00:34:38Z, so the path is no longer dirty and the acknowledgement suppressed nothing. check_round_recorded reported it as a dead entry that 'reads as coverage', which is the fifth gap shape, and deletion is that shape's prescribed remedy.
languages/whence/SECURITY.md.why_this_record_exists: The entry's own landing_violations_note (round 475) says the prescribed remedy destroys the only machine-readable trace that the path was ever adjudicated. Round 484 obeys the remedy and keeps the trace: this key is not read by load_escalated_diffs/classify_escalated_diffs (they read `escalations` only), so it suppresses nothing and cannot be mistaken for a live acknowledgement.

substance_did_not_disappear.note: The same commit that reverted SECURITY.md ADDED a new 120-line security document and committed it. Round 349's mitigation -- 'nothing has been published while it sits in the working tree' -- no longer holds: this one is in git. Round 484 re-checked round 349's four claims against the tree at HEAD; all four are still false (no .pre-commit-config.yaml and the only pre-commit hook is escalationguard.py, which scans no secrets; no .github/workflows; 0 git tags; no .env/*.key patterns in any .gitignore). ONE of the four reappears in the new file, as a green tick: section 6's 'Vulnerability scanning | OK | Up-to-date as of 2026-09-04', which section 7 then contradicts by recommending 'Add automated security scan to GitHub Actions'. The new file also carries a NEW falsifiable claim -- 'Verified test count: 875/875 tests passed' -- against 2802 collected at HEAD and 2682 passed / 4 skipped at round 483's health check; 875 matches no measurement in this repo's record. Its section-3 claim 'No file system access' was checked and HOLDS (no open()/shutil/Path IO anywhere in languages/whence/whence/*.py). Round 484 did NOT rewrite the file, for round 349's reason: it is outward-facing, in a domain where the operator has authorship interest, and the decision is the operator's. This is an ESCALATION, not a resolution.
